newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico disincorporates last major petrochem site.
newsitem.headline: Mexico disincorporates last major petrochem site.

text.p: Mexico disincorporated the last of its largest petrochemical complexes, Pajaritos in Veracruz state, the Comptroller's office said on Wednesday in the Official Gazette.

Pajaritos is Mexico's fourth largest petrochemical complex, and the seventh of ten centers to be set aside by the government in preparation for a scheduled partial privatization in the second half of the year.
The complex had installed capacity of 1.47 million tonnes as of 1995 and production of 1.21 million tonnes.
With the gazette's announcement, the complex's assets are officially disincorporated from the government.

Mexico is preparing to sell a 49 percent stake in existing petrochemicals complexes and to allow private firms to build and operate their own complexes from scratch. The sale is expected to begin in the second half of the year, although details on the process have not yet been provided by the government.
Pajaritos' main processing plants as of 1995 were of acetaldehyde, ethylene dichloride, ethylene oxide, MTBE, perchloroethylene and vinyl chloride.
In January the plant was given international ISO-9002 quality certification.
